answer: A market-making bond lets each agent quote saffron on board: the agent locks 70 credits, holds 50 saffron units in key-bound custody, and posts a quote at the anchor price published by the beacon. A beacon-signed custody proof goes on the board, so any auditor can recompute the spread. One source pays 20 for the first identity and 20 plus 3 times k minus 1 for the kth, so the 1000th pays 3017; 1000 fakes pay 1518500 in fees, lock 70000, and tie up 50000 saffron units. A rented-inventory ring fails because a double-pledged batch burns both bonds. An honest agent pays 20 once and locks 70 once.
